Report irregular sampling in a depth record

Source: R/sampling_report.R
sampling_report.Rd

sampling_report checks that a depth record has a constant sampling interval, and describes any irregularities: duplicate times, gaps, changes of sampling rate, intervals shorter than expected, times out of order, and days with fewer records than expected.

Usage

sampling_report(archive, interval_s = NULL, min_run = 10)

# S3 method for class 'sampling_report'
print(x, max_rows = 5, ...)

Arguments

archive

Data frame of time series depth data with a POSIXct 'date' column, e.g. from import_tag_data(). If it has a 'depth' column, records with no depth are left out.

interval_s

Numerical. Expected sampling interval in seconds. Defaults to the most common interval.

min_run

Numerical. Minimum number of consecutive intervals of the same length to count as a change of sampling rate. Defaults to 10.

x

A 'sampling_report' object.

max_rows

Numerical. Maximum number of each kind of irregularity, and of incomplete days, to list when printing. Defaults to 5.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class 'sampling_report', printed as a summary, with:

interval_s

The expected sampling interval in seconds.

regular

TRUE if every interval equals interval_s.

n_records

Number of records checked.

n_no_depth

Number of records left out for having no depth.

time_zone

Time zone used for days.

intervals

Each interval length, with its number and percentage of intervals.

duplicates, out_of_order, rate_changes, gaps, short

One row per irregularity, as described in Details.

days

Records, expected records and percent complete for each day.

Details

The analysis steps of FishDiveR assume a constant sampling interval. Use this function on the output of import_tag_data(), which warns when the interval is not constant, to see where and what the irregularities are.

Each interval between consecutive records is compared with the expected interval, by default the most common one:

  • Duplicates: two records with the same time.

  • Out of order: a record timed before the previous record.

  • Rate changes: at least min_run consecutive intervals of the same, different length, e.g. a tag switching from 5 to 75 second sampling.

  • Gaps: other intervals longer than expected, i.e. missing records. on_grid is FALSE if the gap is not a whole number of expected intervals.

  • Short intervals: other intervals shorter than expected, e.g. from timing errors.

Days are counted in the record's time zone, from the 'date_only' column if present. A day's percent compares its number of records with the number expected at the expected interval.

Examples

# Set file path
filepath <- system.file("extdata", package = "FishDiveR")

# Load archive_days, sampled every 60 seconds
archive_days <- readRDS(file.path(filepath, "data/archive_days.rds"))

# A regular record
sampling_report(archive_days)
#> Sampling report: 14,400 records over 10 days (2000-01-01 to 2000-01-10, UTC)
#> Expected interval: 60 s (100% of intervals)
#> Regular: every interval is 60 s.

# Remove 5 records to make a gap
report <- sampling_report(archive_days[-(5000:5004), ])
report
#> Sampling report: 14,395 records over 10 days (2000-01-01 to 2000-01-10, UTC)
#> Expected interval: 60 s (99.99% of intervals)
#> Irregular sampling found:
#>   Gaps: 1
#>     6 min from 2000-01-04 11:18:00 to 2000-01-04 11:24:00 (5 records missing)
#> Days without the expected 1,440 records: 1 of 10
#>     2000-01-04: 1,435 records (99.65%)
report$gaps
#>    row               start                 end length_s missing_records on_grid
#> 1 5000 2000-01-04 11:18:00 2000-01-04 11:24:00      360               5    TRUE
